operations.name: James F. Hitselberger

expected.name: James F. Hitselberger
expected.description: James F. Hitselberger is a former Navy contract linguist who worked with the Fifth Fleet in Bahrain. Military investigators accused him in 2012 of taking classified documents from a secure work area; one document was later found in the Hoover Institution archives at Stanford University. Prosecutors initially charged him under the Espionage Act with unauthorized retention of national-defense information. He spent 54 days without bond in the District of Columbia jail before a judge released him on December 19, 2012 to strict home confinement and electronic monitoring. In April 2014 the government replaced the Espionage Act charge with a misdemeanor count of unauthorized removal and retention of classified documents. Hitselberger pleaded guilty and was sentenced on July 17, 2014 to time served and a $250 fine.

operations.research_note: FBI Special Agent Marcus Andre Morgan original sworn criminal-complaint affidavit, filed August6,2012, Document1-1 page1 (PDFpage2), explicitly identifies defendant DOB12/7/56. US month/day format: December7,1956. Exact DOB, not inferred from age.

expected.description: Jack Schneider was a leader of the International Fur and Leather Workers Union who was targeted during a federal deportation drive against labor organizers. updates.description: Jack Schneider was a leader of the International Fur and Leather Workers Union who was targeted during a federal deportation drive against labor organizers. He was detained in civil immigration proceedings, including after his bail was revoked on October 25, 1950. He was released on administrative bail and was arrested again on October 24, 1952, then held without bail. In December 1952, a federal judge ruled that the decision to rearrest and hold him without bail was an abuse of discretion.
